A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Attn-QAT work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and language-model experiments, training ablations, a 99-prompt human evaluation, and RTX 5090 kernel benchmarks.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds B200/GB300 throughput measurements, kernel latency and numerical-error comparisons, and training-overhead findings.

M1.justification: v1 leaves datacenter inference kernels as future work. v3 introduces a CuTe-DSL implementation with mixed-precision QK/PV paths and a TMEM overlap schedule (Section 2.5, Appendix B). This substantially extends inference procedures, while the core QAT training algorithm remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The video-generation and language-model datasets and tasks remain unchanged, including VBench, C4, Dolci-Instruct, and the retained language benchmark suites. The new kernel experiments vary hardware, tensor configurations, and precision within attention benchmarking; they do not introduce different represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated BF16 FlashAttention-4 comparisons in the datacenter kernel benchmarks; v1 only discussed FA4 as a future implementation basis. The original model-quality comparator sets and RTX 5090 comparisons against FlashAttention2 and SageAttention3 are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds noncausal B200/GB300 benchmark protocols with multiple precision combinations, tensor configurations, and cosine/max/mean error measurements against BF16 (Figure 6, Tables 6–7). Figure 6 uses 32 heads on B200 and 24 on GB300. Appendix C.2 also changes the stated Qwen continued-pretraining model from 8B to 14B, aligning with the retained main text without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial analyses of block-scaled PV slowdowns, numerical fidelity across precision combinations and tensor shapes, and training computation/memory/time overhead (Appendices B–C). These examine operating limits and implementation tradeoffs absent from v1. The original backward-design and outlier-mitigation ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for the reported comparisons. The new mean/max absolute errors quantify kernel discrepancies, not statistical uncertainty; the human-evaluation reporting is retained.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–4 and the original quantitative plots are unchanged. v3 adds substantial kernel results: NVFP4 QK plus FP8 PV reaches 2026 TFLOPS on B200 and 2677 TFLOPS on GB300, reported as 1.31x and 1.74x over their respective BF16 FA4 comparisons. Tables 6–7 add latency/error results, and Appendix C.1 reports approximately 1.2x–2x training slowdown.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, STE equations, softmax-gradient derivation, and auxiliary-output identity are retained. Corrections to indexed variables in Algorithms 1–2 and an algorithm-line reference fix notation and cross-referencing without changing the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central novelty, backward-stability principles, and quality-recovery claims are retained. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the efficiency contribution to implemented datacenter kernels and up to 1.74x acceleration over FA4 on GB300, replacing the earlier future-work status.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the interpretation of efficiency limits: softmax throughput and scale computation can negate FP4 GEMM benefits, explaining PV slowdowns and hardware-dependent gains. It adds paged-attention and MXFP8 configuration limitations, training-cost tradeoffs, and a hypothesis that QAT improves robustness to quantization noise without substantially changing attention-logit distributions.

D1.justification: v3 adds detailed datacenter kernel instructions, tile and memory layouts, synchronization scheduling, quantization backends, and training-overhead accounting. It supplies code-access links and reports released kernels where v1 promised future release. Most original training hyperparameters are retained in Appendix C, relocated from Appendix B.

R1.justification: v3 develops the relationship to FA4 from a planned implementation basis into an implemented extension and discussion of asymmetric hardware scaling. It adds CuTe-DSL and kernel-resource citations and refines the fused-attention motivation; the broader PTQ/QAT positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 corrects grammar, terminology, and cross-references, revises the conclusion and part of related work, adds disclosures, and inserts a kernel appendix while moving the training setup to Appendix C.

P2.justification: New throughput plots, the TMEM scheduling diagram, and hardware/latency/error tables substantially expand the visual explanation of implementation and performance tradeoffs (Figure 6, Figure 10, Tables 5–7). Existing displays are rearranged; the qualitative examples remain the same and are renumbered from Figures 6–8 to Figures 7–9.

improvement.justification: v3 turns the explicitly deferred datacenter kernel into a documented and evaluated component, with numerical-fidelity checks and negative latency results that clarify when low precision helps or hurts. Added training-cost accounting and code-access information substantially strengthen practical validation and reproducibility information. Downstream accuracy evidence remains unchanged, and the headline datacenter gains use NVFP4 QK with FP8 PV; the improvement rests on stronger implementation evidence and clearer tradeoffs.
